title: Beetroot, walnut and feta fritters with garlicky kale

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is whole food or a plain staple: beetroot, eggs, flour, walnuts, feta, kale, garlic, Greek yoghurt and bread.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday Tesco item at a normal price, including the walnuts and feta.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, sieve, bowl and frying pan, and shallow-frying fritters is well within a confident beginner's reach.

works.reason: 500g beetroot bound with 2 eggs and 100g flour, with walnuts, feta, kale, yoghurt and bread, makes a sensible dinner for four, and the frying time suits coarsely grated raw beetroot.

honest_times.reason: Peeling and grating the beetroot, frying in batches and wilting the kale fit comfortably within the 50 minutes printed in total.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the cumin and lemon, appears in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: The beetroot is the body of the fritters and the dish is a hot, filling winter dinner that suits early December.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or health preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Vegetable fritters with eggs, nuts and cheese, plus greens, yoghurt and bread, make a proper, appealing family meal.
